title: Dem Bones
description: Dem Bones (Dry Bones) in Tonic Solfa: the toe bone connected to the foot bone, with the solfa under the words, staff notation and a piano.
about: Dem Bones, also called Dry Bones, is a spiritual on Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones (Ezekiel 37), credited to the brothers James Weldon Johnson and J. Rosamond Johnson and first recorded in 1928.

verses.label: Chorus
lines: Dem bones, dem bones, dem dry bones,
Dem bones, dem bones, dem dry bones,
Dem bones, dem bones, dem dry bones,
Now hear the word of the Lord.
Toe bone connected to the foot bone,
Foot bone connected to the heel bone,
Heel bone connected to the ankle bone,
Ankle bone connected to the leg bone,
Leg bone connected to the knee bone,
Knee bone connected to the thigh bone,
Thigh bone connected to the hip bone,
Hip bone connected to the back bone,
Back bone connected to the shoulder bone,
Shoulder bone connected to the neck bone,
Neck bone connected to the head bone,
Now hear the word of the Lord.

verses.label: Chorus
lines: Dem bones, dem bones gonna walk around,
Dem bones, dem bones gonna walk around,
Dem bones, dem bones gonna walk around,
Now hear the word of the Lord.

reviewNotes: DRAFT, not published: its tune (tunes/dem-bones.json) has no melody, because no public-domain score of the 1928 song was found to read one from, and a melody written from memory would be published as the authoritative one. The words are the commonly sung ones (as Wikipedia gives them), not checked against the Johnsons' 1928 text; the verse is often sung back down ('Head bone connected to the neck bone …'). To publish: add the melody to the tune, an underlay for the first verse, check the words and dates against the 1928 publication, set "draft": false. The credits (words to James Weldon Johnson, music to both brothers) follow Wikipedia; some sources call the words traditional — check.
